00098| ## Summary: Yazi Config Syntax Issues Found
00099| 
00100| Based on my investigation of current yazi documentation and your config, I've identified the root cause of why pressing "O" isn't showing your configured openers. **The syntax has changed significantly in yazi version 25.12.29+ (you're running 26.1.22).**

00103| 
00104| Your current config uses:
00105| ```toml

00109| **This is incorrect in Yazi 26.1.22.** According to the [official Yazi documentation](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/), the `[open]` section only supports two matching types:
00110| - `url`: Glob expression for matching filenames (e.g., `*.py`, `*/`)
00111| - `mime`: Glob expression for matching MIME types (e.g., `text/*`, `image/*`)
00112| 
00113| The `inode/directory` MIME type is technically valid and may work, but it's not the modern Yazi way. The current pattern used in recent yazi examples is `name = "*/"` for directories, but this reveals another issue.
00114| 
00115| ### Breaking Change: `name` → `url` Rename
00116| 
00117| According to the [Yazi changelog](https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) (version 25.12.29+), **`name` was renamed to `url`** across all rule types to support virtual filesystems ([GitHub issue #3034](https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/issues/3034)).
00118| 
00119| Many example configurations still use the old `name = "*/"` syntax for directories, but this **no longer works** in Yazi 26.1. The correct modern syntax is:
00120| ```toml
00121| { url = "*/", use = ["edit", "git", "marimo_dir", "agent", "open"] }
00122| ```
00123| 
00124| ### Correct Modern Syntax for Your Config
00125| 
00126| Based on the [official documentation](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/) and [example configurations](https://github.com/mingo99/yazi.config), your `[open]` section should be:
00127| 
00128| ```toml
00129| [open]
00130| rules = [
00131|   # Directories: multiple openers to choose from with O
00132|   { url = "*/", use = ["edit", "git", "marimo_dir", "agent", "open"] },
00133|   
00134|   # Python files
00135|   { url = "*.py", use = ["edit", "marimo_py_sandbox", "open", "code"] },
00136|   
00137|   # Text/code files
00138|   { mime = "text/*", use = ["edit", "open", "code"] },
00139|   
00140|   # Everything else
00141|   { mime = "*", use = ["open"] },
00142| ]
00143| ```
00144|

00205| 
00206| ## Yazi Opener Configuration Syntax
00207| 
00208| The `[opener]` section in yazi.toml configures available openers that can be used in file opening operations, with entries like `play` and `edit` containing arrays of opener definitions.
00209| 
00210| ### Basic Opener Structure
00211| 
00212| Each opener is an object with properties including `run` (the command to execute), `orphan` (boolean for whether to keep the process running after Yazi exits), `block` (boolean for blocking manner), `for` (platform specification like "unix" or "windows"), and `desc` (description for display in interactive components).
00213| 
00214| ### Key Properties
00215| 
00216| - `block`: Opens in a blocking manner, hiding Yazi into a secondary screen and displaying the program on the main screen until it exits, allowing it to receive I/O signals
00217| 
00218| - `orphan`: Keeps the process running even if Yazi has exited; once specified, the process is detached from the task scheduling system
00219| 
00220| - `desc`: Description of the opener, displayed in interactive components like "Open with" and help menu
00221| 
00222| ### Example
00223| 
00224| A simple example shows: `[opener]` with `open = [ { run = "xdg-open %s", desc = "Open" }, ]`
00225| 
00226| The `%s` placeholder represents the file path being opened. You can define multiple openers for different file types and use `for` to specify platform-specific commands.
00227|

00327| Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about configuring open rules with mime types and openers in yazi.toml:
00328| 
00329| ## Open Rules Configuration
00330| 
00331| The [open] section defines rules that map file types to openers defined in the [opener] section. Rules are matched against file names and MIME types.
00332| 
00333| ### Configuration Methods
00334| 
00335| Yazi provides three ways to configure opening rules: Extend defaults with prepend_rules and append_rules, or use `rules` to completely override the defaults.
00336| 
00337| ### Rule Options
00338| 
00339| For each rule, you can specify:
00340| 
00341| - **url** (String): Glob expression for matching the file URL. Case-insensitive by default, add \s to the beginning to make it sensitive.
00342| 
00343| - **mime** (String): Glob expression for matching the mime-type. Case-insensitive by default, add \s to the beginning to make it sensitive.
00344| 
00345| - **cond** (String): Conditional expression – Only rules that meet this condition and satisfy either the url or mime will be applied. For example, A & B means A and B, and A | !B means A or not B.
00346| 
00347| - **use** (String or Array of strings, Required): Opener name(s) from the [opener] section.
00348| 
00349| ### Multiple Openers
00350| 
00351| If use is an array containing multiple openers, all commands in these openers will be merged. open will run the first of these commands; open --interactive will list all of these commands in the "open with" menu.
00352| 
00353| ### Example Configuration
00354| 
00355| You can use rules to rewrite the entire default rules: [open] rules = [ { mime = "text/*", use = "edit" }, { mime = "video/*", use = "play" },
00356| 
00357| Or with `prepend_rules` and `append_rules`:
00358| 
00359| You can prepend or append rules to the default through prepend_rules and append_rules: [open] prepend_rules = [ { url = "*.json", use = "edit" }, { url = "*.html", use = [ "open", "edit" ] }, ]
00360|

00379| ## About Yazi
00380| 
00381| Yazi (means "duck") is a terminal file manager written in Rust, based on non-blocking async I/O. It aims to provide an efficient, user-friendly, and customizable file management experience.
00382| 
00383| ## Recent Version
00384| 
00385| The current version is 26.1.22, based on the official documentation.
00386| 
00387| ## Opener Definition
00388| 
00389| In Yazi's configuration system, an **opener** is a customizable command used to open files. Opener name corresponds to the names in the [opener] section of the configuration file. If use is an array containing multiple openers, all commands in these openers will be merged; open will run the first of these commands; open --interactive will list all of these commands in the "open with" menu.
00390| 
00391| Openers allow you to define how different file types are opened based on their MIME type, giving you flexibility in choosing applications to handle specific file formats.

00704|      1→# 35_yazi.zsh - yazi file manager configuration

00706|      3→# Check if yazi is installed
00707|      4→command -v yazi &>/dev/null || return 0
00708|      5→
00709|      6→# Wrapper function to change directory on exit
00710|      7→# When you quit yazi, it will cd to the directory you were browsing
00711|      8→function y() {
00712|      9→    local tmp="$(mktemp -t "yazi-cwd.XXXXXX")" cwd
00713|     10→    command yazi "$@" --cwd-file="$tmp"
00714|     11→    IFS= read -r -d '' cwd < "$tmp"
00715|     12→    [ "$cwd" != "$PWD" ] && [ -d "$cwd" ] && builtin cd -- "$cwd"
00716|     13→    rm -f -- "$tmp"
00717|     14→}
00718|     15→
00719| ```

00771|     43→    Bootstrap --> Chezmoi --> Ansible
00772|     44→    Chezmoi -.-> BrewBundle
00773|     45→    MISE -.->|Node.js, Rust| NVIM
00774|     46→    MISE -.->|Rust| CARGO
00775|     47→    UV -.->|Python tools| UVTOOLS
00776|     48→    BREW -.->|casks| CASKS
00777|     49→```
00778|     50→
00779|     51→## Quick Setup
00780|     52→
00781|     53→```bash
00782|     54→# One-liner to initialize and apply (installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin)
00783|     55→export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
00784|     56→sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
00785|     57→```
00786|     58→
00787|     59→This automatically:
00788|     60→
00789|     61→1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
00790|     62→2. Deploys all config files
00791|     63→3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
00792|     64→4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` enabled)
00793|     65→
00794|     66→### Optional Components
00795|     67→
00796|     68→During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs:
00797|     69→
00798|     70→| Option | Default | Description |
00799|     71→|--------|---------|-------------|
00800|     72→| `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, td, sidecar, specify-cli, etc. |
00801|     73→| `installBitwarden` | false | Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) + Desktop app (desktop profiles) with SSH agent auto-detection |
00802|     74→| `installPythonUvTools` | true | Python CLI tools via uv (mlflow, litellm, sqlit-tui, etc.) |
00803|     75→| `installBrewApps` | false | GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (casks, mas) |
00804|     76→| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |
00805|     77→
00806|     78→To change options later: `chezmoi init --force`
00807|     79→
00808|     80→## What You Get
00809|     81→
00810|     82→### Config Files
00811|     83→
00812|     84→- `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration
00813|     85→- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration
00814|     86→- `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config
00815|     87→- `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry mirror config (GFW)
00816|     88→- `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
00817|     89→- `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
00818|     90→- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config
00819|     91→- `~/.config/yazi/yazi.toml` - Yazi file manager open rules and openers (`o`/`O`)
00820|     92→- `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
00821|     93→- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins
00822|     94→- `~/.local/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `paste` / `open`
00823|     95→- `~/.config/zsh/tools/36_pueue.zsh` - Pueue queue summary helper (`pqsum`)
00824|     96→- `~/.config/zsh/tools/28_tldr.zsh` - `tldrf` helper with `TLDR_LANGUAGES` fallback order
00825|     97→- `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` - Bitwarden CLI completion + SSH agent socket auto-detection
00826|     98→- `~/.ssh/config` - SSH main config skeleton (create-only: `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` + conservative `Host *` defaults)
00827|     99→- `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` - SSH global defaults stub (commented examples only)
00828|    100→- `~/.ssh/config.d/git` - SSH host entries for `github.com` and `gitlab.com` with commented multi-account/Bitwarden examples
00829| ```

01723| ```text
01724| # [opener] and [open] Sections Syntax
01725| 
01726| ## [opener] Section
01727| 
01728| Define available programs to open files:
01729| 
01730| ```toml
01731| [opener]
01732| play = [
01733|   { run = "mpv %s", orphan = true, for = "unix" },
01734|   { run = '"C:\Program Files\mpv.exe" %s', orphan = true, for = "windows" }
01735| ]
01736| edit = [
01737|   { run = "$EDITOR %s", block = true, for = "unix" },
01738|   { run = "%EDITOR% %s", block = true, for = "windows" }
01739| ]
01740| open = [
01741|   { run = "xdg-open %s", desc = "Open" }
01742| ]
01743| ```
01744| 
01745| **Options:**
01746| - `run`: Command with formatting parameters (`%s`, `%S`, `%sN`, `%SN`, `%d`, `%D`, etc.)
01747| - `block`: Hide Yazi and display program on main screen until exit
01748| - `orphan`: Keep process running after Yazi closes
01749| - `desc`: Human-readable description
01750| - `for`: System availability (`linux`, `macos`, `windows`, `android`, `unix`)
01751| 
01752| ## [open] Section
01753| 
01754| Set rules for opening specific file types:
01755| 
01756| ```toml
01757| [open]
01758| prepend_rules = [
01759|   { url = "*.json", use = "edit" },
01760|   { url = "*.html", use = [ "open", "edit" ] }
01761| ]
01762| append_rules = [
01763|   { url = "*", use = "my-fallback" }
01764| ]
01765| ```
01766| 
01767| Or rewrite entirely:
01768| 
01769| ```toml
01770| [open]
01771| rules = [
01772|   { mime = "text/*", use = "edit" },
01773|   { mime = "video/*", use = "play" },
01774|   { url = "*.json", use = "edit" }
01775| ]
01776| ```
01777| 
01778| **Rule options:**
01779| - `url`: Glob pattern for filenames (case-insensitive by default; prefix with `\s` for sensitivity)
01780| - `mime`: Glob pattern for MIME types
01781| - `use`: Opener name(s) from `[opener]` section
01782| ```
01783| </details></tool-use>

01792| # Yazi.toml Opener and Open Rules Configuration
01793| 
01794| Based on the GitHub repository content, here's the complete configuration:
01795| 
01796| ## Openers Section
01797| 
01798| ```toml
01799| [opener]
01800| edit = [
01801|  { run = 'nvim "$@"', desc = "nvim", block = true, for = "unix" },
01802|  { run = 'code %*', orphan = true, desc = "code", for = "windows" },
01803|  { run = 'code -w %*', block = true, desc = "code (block)", for = "windows" },
01804| ]
01805| 
01806| open = [
01807|  { run = 'xdg-open "$1"', desc = "Open", for = "linux" },
01808|  { run = 'open "$@"', desc = "Open", for = "macos" },
01809|  { run = 'start "" "%1"', orphan = true, desc = "Open", for = "windows" },
01810| ]
01811| 
01812| reveal = [
01813|  { run = 'xdg-open "$(dirname "$1")"', desc = "Reveal", for = "linux" },
01814|  { run = 'open -R "$1"', desc = "Reveal", for = "macos" },
01815|  { run = 'explorer /select,"%1"', orphan = true, desc = "Reveal", for = "windows" },
01816| ]
01817| 
01818| extract = [
01819|  { run = 'ya pub extract --list "$@"', desc = "Extract here", for = "unix" },
01820|  { run = 'ya pub extract --list %*', desc = "Extract here", for = "windows" },
01821| ]
01822| 
01823| play = [
01824|  { run = 'mpv --force-window "$@"', orphan = true, for = "unix" },
01825|  { run = 'mpv --force-window %*', orphan = true, for = "windows" },
01826| ]
01827| ```
01828| 
01829| ## Open Rules Section
01830| 
01831| ```toml
01832| [open]
01833| rules = [
01834|  { name = "*/", use = ["edit", "open", "reveal"] },

02435| Based on the search results, here's the difference between `"name"` and `"url"` in Yazi mime rules:
02436| 
02437| ## Key Differences
02438| 
02439| **url**: A glob expression for matching the file URL (the file path/filename pattern). **mime**: A glob expression for matching the mime-type.
02440| 
02441| ## Practical Usage
02442| 
02443| The distinction becomes clear in practical examples:
02444| 
02445| - For preview rules, both url and mime patterns are used as glob expressions to match files
02446| - In theme filetype rules, you can use mime patterns like "image/*" for broad categories, while url patterns like "*/" match directories or "*" matches any file
02447| 
02448| ## When to Use Each
02449| 
02450| - **Use `url`** when you want to match by filename pattern (e.g., `"*.raf"`, `"*.json"`, `"*/"`). For example, SVG files can be matched specifically with `name = "*.svg"` while other image types are matched by mime type.
02451| 
02452| - **Use `mime`** when you want to match by file content type (e.g., `"image/*"`, `"text/*"`, `"application/pdf"`). This is more reliable than extension-based matching since it's based on actual file content.
02453| 
02454| In icon configuration, there's also a `"name"` field (separate from `url`) used specifically for directory and file name matching in the icon section.
02455|

02602| 
02603| The key points about this syntax are:
02604| 
02605| - The pattern `"*/"` matches all directories
02606| - The `name` field uses a glob expression for matching file names
02607| - The `use` field specifies opener name(s) from the [opener] section
02608| 
02609| The `*/` pattern is a glob pattern specifically designed to match directories by including the trailing slash, distinguishing them from regular files which would use just `*`.

02873| # Yazi [open] Section Syntax
02874| 
02875| Based on the documentation, the `[open]` section uses **`url`** and **`mime`** for matching rules, not inode or directory-specific patterns.
02876| 
02877| ## Rule Structure
02878| 
02879| ```toml
02880| [open]
02881| rules = [
02882|     { mime = "text/*", use = "edit" },
02883|     { mime = "video/*", use = "play" },
02884|     { url = "*.json", use = "edit" },
02885|     { url = "*.html", use = [ "open", "edit" ] },
02886| ]
02887| ```
02888| 
02889| ## Available Matching Options
02890| 
02891| - **`url`**: "Glob expression for matching the file URL. Case-insensitive by default"
02892| - **`mime`**: "Glob expression for matching the mime-type"
02893| - **`use`**: References opener names from `[opener]` section (can be string or array)
02894| 
02895| ## Key Note on Directories
02896| 
02897| The documentation does not provide directory-specific matching capabilities. Pattern matching relies solely on file URLs (glob expressions) and MIME types. To identify a directory's contents, you would check its MIME type, which typically returns `inode/directory` for folder objects in Unix-like systems, but Yazi's configuration syntax doesn't explicitly document this approach.

02905| ## Summary: Yazi Config Syntax Issues Found
02906| 
02907| Based on my investigation of current yazi documentation and your config, I've identified the root cause of why pressing "O" isn't showing your configured openers. **The syntax has changed significantly in yazi version 25.12.29+ (you're running 26.1.22).**
02908| 
02909| ### Critical Issue: `mime = "inode/directory"` is the Problem
02910| 
02911| Your current config uses:
02912| ```toml
02913| { mime = "inode/directory", use = ["edit", "git", "marimo_dir", "agent", "open"] }
02914| ```
02915| 
02916| **This is incorrect in Yazi 26.1.22.** According to the [official Yazi documentation](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/), the `[open]` section only supports two matching types:
02917| - `url`: Glob expression for matching filenames (e.g., `*.py`, `*/`)
02918| - `mime`: Glob expression for matching MIME types (e.g., `text/*`, `image/*`)
02919| 
02920| The `inode/directory` MIME type is technically valid and may work, but it's not the modern Yazi way. The current pattern used in recent yazi examples is `name = "*/"` for directories, but this reveals another issue.
02921| 
02922| ### Breaking Change: `name` → `url` Rename
02923| 
02924| According to the [Yazi changelog](https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) (version 25.12.29+), **`name` was renamed to `url`** across all rule types to support virtual filesystems ([GitHub issue #3034](https://github.com/sxyazi/yazi/issues/3034)).
02925| 
02926| Many example configurations still use the old `name = "*/"` syntax for directories, but this **no longer works** in Yazi 26.1. The correct modern syntax is:
02927| ```toml
02928| { url = "*/", use = ["edit", "git", "marimo_dir", "agent", "open"] }
02929| ```
02930| 
02931| ### Correct Modern Syntax for Your Config
02932| 
02933| Based on the [official documentation](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/yazi/) and [example configurations](https://github.com/mingo99/yazi.config), your `[open]` section should be:
02934| 
02935| ```toml
02936| [open]
02937| rules = [
02938|   # Directories: multiple openers to choose from with O
02939|   { url = "*/", use = ["edit", "git", "marimo_dir", "agent", "open"] },
02940|   
02941|   # Python files
02942|   { url = "*.py", use = ["edit", "marimo_py_sandbox", "open", "code"] },
02943|   
02944|   # Text/code files
02945|   { mime = "text/*", use = ["edit", "open", "code"] },
02946|   
02947|   # Everything else
02948|   { mime = "*", use = ["open"] },
02949| ]
02950| ```
02951|

02953| 
02954| 1. **`mime = "inode/directory"` → `url = "*/"`** - Use the glob pattern for directories instead of MIME type
02955| 2. **All other rules work correctly** - Your `mime` patterns are fine
02956| 3. **Openers section looks good** - No changes needed there

02959| 
02960| When you press "O" on a directory in Yazi:
02961| - Old behavior (your current config): Tries to match `inode/directory` MIME type, which may not work reliably
02962| - New behavior (corrected config): Matches `url = "*/"` pattern, explicitly targeting all directories and providing all configured openers

03067| # [open] Section Documentation
03068| 
03069| ## Syntax for Matching Files and Directories
03070| 
03071| The `[open]` section uses two primary matching methods:
03072| 
03073| 1. **`url`**: "Glob expression for matching the file URL. Case-insensitive by default, add `\s` to the beginning to make it sensitive."
03074|

03079| ## Opener Rules Examples
03080| 
03081| Basic rule structure:
03082| 
03083| ```toml
03084| [open]
03085| prepend_rules = [
03086|     { url = "*.json", use = "edit" },
03087|     { url = "*.html", use = [ "open", "edit" ] },
03088| ]
03089| ```
03090| 
03091| Key points:
03092| - The `use` field can reference single openers or arrays of multiple openers
03093| - When `use` contains multiple openers, "all commands in these openers will be merged"
03094| - "open will run the first of these commands; open --interactive will list all of these commands in the 'open with' menu"
03095| 
03096| ## Configuration Organization
03097| 
03098| Three approaches are supported:
03099| - `prepend_rules`: Adds custom rules before defaults
03100| - `append_rules`: Adds custom rules after defaults  
03101| - `rules`: Completely replaces default rules

03128| # Breaking Changes in Yazi v25.12.29: Open Rules Syntax
03129| 
03130| Based on the changelog, here are the critical breaking changes affecting open rules configuration:
03131| 
03132| ## 1. **Field Rename: "name" → "url"**
03133| 
03134| In v25.12.29, a major refactoring renamed the `name` field to `url` across multiple rule types to support the new virtual file system:
03135| 
03136| > "Rename `name` to `url` for open, fetchers, spotters, preloaders, previewers, filetype, and `globs` icon rules"
03137| 
03138| This change applies to:
03139| - Open rules
03140| - Fetchers
03141| - Spotters
03142| - Preloaders
03143| - Previewers
03144| - Filetype rules
03145| - Globs icon rules
03146| 
03147| ## 2. **Removal of $0 Parameter in Opener Rules**
03148| 
03149| A significant change in v25.12.29 eliminated the `$0` variable:
03150| 
03151| > "Remove `$0` parameter in opener rules to make the `open` command work under empty directories"
03152| 
03153| This enables the `open` command to function even when no files are selected in empty directories.
03154| 
03155| ## 3. **Shell Formatting Deprecation**
03156| 
03157| Variables like `$n`, `$@` (*nix) and `%n`, `%*` (Windows) in shell commands and opener rules are deprecated in favor of new shell formatting syntax introduced in v25.5.28.
03158| 
03159| ## Migration Path
03160| 
03161| Users upgrading to v25.12.29 or later must update their `open` section in configuration files, replacing `name` with `url` and removing `$0` references where applicable.
03162| ```

03202| 2. Using the **URL glob pattern** method (`url = */`)
